solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some papers cover shareholder's meeting to unearth muck

indicators.note: the papers cover the meeting, wrapping round it

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM = annual general meeting, where shareholders gather

explanation.surface: An investigative journalist promises to dig the dirt at a company's annual meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unearth muck' sounds like exposing scandal, but muck is simply mire, the definition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym by way of mire: a bog is ground so soft it is all mud, which is what muck means here.

clue.text: Throw a square cut at source of radiation

indicators.note: 'square cut' is SQUARE with its end chopped off
to throw the letters is to toss them into a new order

parts.note: SQUARE loses its last letter, E

explanation.surface: A craftsman rages and hurls a cut square of material at a glowing heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square cut' reads like a cricket shot or a joiner's cut; here it just trims one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A quasar is a distant galaxy core pouring out enormous amounts of radiation.

clue.text: I am enthralled by a country's cartoon

indicators.note: held captive inside the country

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being captivated by a nation's famous cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Read country's as 'country is': the setter's apostrophe lets the enthralled pair sit inside the nation rather than beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a cartoon is a drawn film, and animation is the name for that kind of film.

clue.text: Dull time when both sides have winning position

indicators.note: the winning position stands on both sides of the time letter, enclosing it

parts.note: checkmate, the winning position in chess

explanation.surface: A tedious sports match in which each side thinks it has the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both sides have winning position' sounds like a stalemate; it means MATE wraps round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym from paint and photo paper, where the choice is gloss or a flat, lustreless finish.

clue.text: Tortoise almost smashed dish

indicators.note: almost all of TORTOISE, missing its last letter
smashed to pieces and put back differently

explanation.surface: A tortoise lumbers across a kitchen and very nearly breaks a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like the crockery being smashed; it is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Italian rice cooked slowly in stock is served as a dish in its own right.

clue.text: Turn to block some water?

indicators.note: the turn goes in to block the water, sitting inside it

parts.note: spit is a little water from the mouth, hence the question mark
a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

explanation.surface: A plumber asks which way to turn a valve to shut off the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the thing you turn to stop a flow; spit is a fair if cheeky example of some water, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a tap or plug on a cask or pipe, turned to stop or release the flow.

clue.text: Ape eats cow next

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater

explanation.surface: A zoo report: the ape will devour a cow next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next' looks like the end of the story; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest or next in order.

clue.text: Good to flatten pasture

parts.note: to raze is to level to the ground

explanation.surface: A farmer decides it is a good idea to roll the field flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasture' is a verb here: to put animals out to feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: putting animals out on grass to feed, or their feeding there.

clue.text: Fortune teller first gives comfort with limited success

indicators.note: the S of success is held back, so REASSURE keeps just one S
the teller's first letter only

explanation.surface: A fortune teller tries to reassure clients, with only modest success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fortune teller' is a single phrase in the surface, but it splits: Fortune is the definition and teller supplies T.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a hoard of gold and jewels is a great store of wealth, which is the money sense of fortune.

clue.text: It really discriminates against a trial involving detectives

indicators.note: the trial involves, so contains, the detectives

parts.note: CID = Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: A complaint that a police-led trial is deeply biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discriminates' suggests prejudice; the definition means telling true from false, which is the older, neutral sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from assaying: nitric acid told real gold from fake, so the phrase came to mean any decisive proof.

clue.text: Desert island loses border to east after short time

parts.note: E = east, replacing Java's last A

explanation.surface: A desert island erodes away at its eastern edge after a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert island' is a stock phrase that must be split: Desert is the definition, island is JAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mojave is a desert in the south-western United States.

clue.text: One could be stuck up or sticky after removal of additives

indicators.note: the additives are taken out of the sticky sweet

parts.note: E numbers are food additives, so two Es

explanation.surface: Something might end up glued in place, or merely tacky once the additives are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: E numbers are the codes for food additives on European labels, so additives are Es. A toff is an upper-class British person.
explanation.definitionFit: A toff is a snob, someone who could be stuck-up.

clue.text: Conscious of needing a wash

parts.note: a boat's wash is its wake

explanation.surface: Someone is self-consciously aware that they need a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash' is the water churned up behind a boat, not a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: alert to a danger or fact, with 'of' matching the 'to' that follows in use.

clue.text: Cheats double-crossing king

indicators.note: the king is crossed by, so set inside, the double

explanation.surface: Traitors who double-cross the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double-crossing' is one word in the surface but splits in two: double gives TWO TIMES and crossing puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: people unfaithful to a partner, seeing someone else on the side.

clue.text: Samples from anorak I monopolise to manufacture robe

indicators.note: a sample is a piece taken out of the phrase

parts.note: the letters run from the end of anorak across I into the start of monopolise

explanation.surface: A garment maker hogs all the anorak fabric to make a dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anorak' tempts you to think of clothing, and the robe is indeed clothing, but the letters are what count.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the wide-sleeved Japanese garment, wrapped and sashed, is a kind of robe.

clue.text: Insecure due to missing first of January, perhaps I visited holiday resort

indicators.note: the month loses its first letter

parts.note: January is an example of a month
Nice, the resort on the French Riviera
surface padding: 'I visited Nice' just sets I beside the resort

explanation.surface: A traveller frets about a January trip to a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of January' looks like New Year's Day, and J is the tempting letter; it is the first letter of the month the example stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a skater on ice that may crack at any moment stands for anyone whose position is shaky.

clue.text: Taste meal — have contents been swallowed?

indicators.note: what is swallowed goes inside the meal

parts.note: meal is coarsely ground grain, a kind of flour

indicators.note: the contents of HAVE are its inner letters

explanation.surface: A diner tastes a meal and wonders whether the food has been eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meal' is ground grain, not dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both nouns: the savour a food leaves on the tongue.

clue.text: Hook was honed and moulded with energy

definitions.note: Captain Hook, having lost a hand to the crocodile, was one-handed

indicators.note: clay that is moulded keeps its material but takes a new form, as these letters do

explanation.surface: A metal hook was sharpened and shaped with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hook' is Captain Hook of Peter Pan, not a metal hook; a definition naming an example is fair here because it reads as a statement about him.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hook had a hook in place of one hand, so he was one-handed.

clue.text: Two strikes number one

explanation.surface: A bowler takes two wickets with successive balls to reach the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two strikes' asks for two words each meaning strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Music-chart idiom: a record at the top of the charts, the number one spot, is a runaway success.

clue.text: Vet for lizard

definitions.meaning: the verb: to check over or keep watch on
a family of large lizards that includes the Komodo dragon

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pet lizard going to the vet; 'Vet' is the verb meaning check.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb for keeping a check on something, and the big lizards of Africa, Asia and Australia, supposedly named for warning of crocodiles.

clue.text: Route travelled by sea was up for discussion

indicators.note: being discussed means being spoken of

parts.note: rowed = travelled over water by oar

explanation.surface: A committee debated which sea route to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was up for discussion' pairs with 'travelled': ROWED is past tense, like 'was'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: any way from one place to another, as in 'the road to Damascus'.

clue.text: Most shoes are listed

definitions.note: a fill-in-the-blank: most shoes are heeled
definitions.meaning: a fill-in-the-blank: what nearly all shoes have under the back of the foot, as an adjective
a ship that lists leans over, or heels

explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed' suggests catalogued; it is the nautical sense of leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: Most shoes have heels, so are heeled, and a ship that has heeled has listed to one side.

clue.text: Save sailor outside port

indicators.note: the sailor goes round the port

parts.note: a USB port on a computer

explanation.surface: A rescue of a sailor stranded just outside a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' is a computer socket, not a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Old verb sense, from managing a household: to use sparingly and so conserve.

clue.text: Handle compiler's rejection the wrong way

indicators.note: read the wrong way, from end to start

parts.note: the compiler (setter) speaking of himself: my

explanation.surface: The setter complains that an editor handled a rejected clue badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' is a noun meaning a name, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a name, and a handle is slang for a name.

clue.text: Weapons crisis at motorway interchange

indicators.note: the letters change places with each other

parts.note: M = motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Road rage at a busy junction escalates until weapons come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motorway interchange' is a stock phrase that splits: motorway gives M and interchange stirs the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: curved single-edged swords of the Middle East, one kind of weapon.

clue.text: Smooths cuffs

definitions.meaning: an iron smooths creases out of clothes
the noun: handcuffs or shackles, as in a prisoner 'clapped in' them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuffs' looks like part of the shirt being ironed; it is the noun for handcuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes smooths them, and irons are fetters or handcuffs.

clue.text: Caught light fixture in bracket

parts.note: a lamp is a light fitting

explanation.surface: A lamp gets caught up in a wall bracket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal; it only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a brace or bracket that holds things together.

clue.text: Some radiation treatment carries electric current

definitions.note: a curie is a unit measuring an amount of radioactivity

indicators.note: the treatment carries the current inside it

parts.note: I is the symbol for current

explanation.surface: A radiotherapy session involves passing a current through the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface is apt: the unit is named after Marie and Pierre Curie, pioneers of radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: A curie is a unit of radioactivity, so one curie is some amount of radiation.

clue.text: Who was suitable to announce walk

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud

parts.note: fit is an American past tense of fit, so 'was suitable' = fit

explanation.surface: A casting director names who was right for the part, then tells the rest to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was suitable' needs the past tense FIT, as in 'the suit fit him'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoof it is slang for going on foot.

clue.text: Scold overwrought pointless article

indicators.note: without a point of the compass, here E

parts.note: HARRIED without E (east, a compass point)

explanation.surface: Someone berates a frantic, useless piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scold' is the noun, a nagging woman, not the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, scolding old woman, as is a scold.

clue.text: One pumps covering at night

definitions.meaning: one who pumps someone for information is testing them
the canopy over a four-poster bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pumps' looks like shoes; it means questions hard, as an examiner does. A tester is also the canopy over a four-poster bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pumps a candidate for answers is a tester, and a tester covers a bed you sleep in at night.

clue.text: Daughter made unfinished nude sculpture's appendage

indicators.note: MADE loses its last letter
sculpture is the letters being reshaped

explanation.surface: A daughter adds a limb to a half-finished nude statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about carving; sculpture's reads as 'sculpture has' and its job is to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both are things attached at the end, though an addendum is usually text added to a document.
